title: Risk-based credibility assessment of two implicit finite element models for external fixator construct stiffness under ASME V&V 40
device: Modular unilateral external fixator for diaphyseal tibial fracture stabilization

models.name: HF-Contact
models.what_it_computes: Implicit finite element model resolving frictional pin–cortex contact, clamp interfaces, and bar–clamp compliance to predict construct stiffness under prescribed loads.

models.name: RB-Beam
models.what_it_computes: Implicit finite element reduced-order model using beam/spring idealization of bars and pins with rigid connectors to predict construct stiffness under prescribed loads.

mechanisms.name: Axial compression across a standardized fracture gap
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Determines interfragmentary motion magnitude along the load axis, influencing callus formation and early stability.

mechanisms.name: Frontal-plane bending (varus–valgus) about the fracture gap
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Controls shear and opening/closing across the gap during mediolateral loading, which affects alignment maintenance and tissue strain environment.

clear_factors: Relevance of the quantities of interest

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported on a 0–5 Credibility Index (CI) per model–mechanism pair, with acceptance defined as CI ≥ 3.0 for the stated medium model risk.

sections: Context of use (CoU): Use of model-predicted construct stiffness to support design verification and preclinical evidence for a modular unilateral external fixator; clinical performance is not directly inferred

Model risk level and rationale: Medium model risk because predictions guide design iteration and bench test planning but are not the sole basis for regulatory clearance or clinical decisions; erroneous outputs are bounded by mandatory mechanical testing and design controls
Computational models: HF-Contact and RB-Beam (implicit analyses, pre- and post-processing workflows)
Mechanisms of interest: Axial compression and frontal-plane bending
Quantities of interest and their relevance to the decision
Equivalency of input parameters between models, physical tests, and device configuration
Numerical solver error assessment for implicit static solutions
Discretization error estimation and mesh convergence procedures
Test samples and loading configurations for mechanism-specific comparisons
Scoring rubric: 0–5 Credibility Index for each factor and model–mechanism pair, acceptance threshold for medium risk
Factor scores by model–mechanism pair (0–5 CI)
Discussion and implications for the stated CoU
